open_points.subject: start_and_recover_kernel / check_installed_instances
open_points.text: State 2 A09 rule 1: "an installation whose credential header has, compared without regard to case, the name of a required header, or of a header the kernel sets itself (A08 rule 5), refuses to start." vs State 4 step 3: "capability:bindings.check_installed_instances: no credential header has, case-insensitively, the name of a required header of its instance (A09 rule 1)."
open_points.question: At start, is a credential-header collision with kernel-set headers also checked and start-refused, and if so in which step/module?
options: Check both required-header and kernel-set-header collisions in bindings.check_installed_instances at start
Check required-header collisions at start, but kernel-set-header collisions only later during send
open_points.default_guess: Check both collision kinds in bindings.check_installed_instances at start, matching A09 rule 1.

open_points.subject: run_read_only_flow / read operation request building with file inputs
open_points.text: State 4 run_read_only_flow step 3 says prepare_request "places the inputs, JSON values as capability:canonical_values.canonical_bytes" but does not name how file inputs are obtained; run_effect_with_approval step 1 explicitly says "file inputs are read through capability:store.read_value_bytes."
open_points.question: When a read-class operation node has file inputs, which module/capability reads file bytes for request construction in run_read_only_flow?
options: effects reads file bytes via store.read_value_bytes before calling service_invoker.prepare_request (same as run_effect_with_approval)
read-class bindings are implicitly disallowed from having file inputs
open_points.default_guess: Use the same path as run_effect_with_approval: effects reads file bytes through store.read_value_bytes.
